cards.text: Jesus has just fed a crowd of about five thousand men, besides women and children (Matthew 14:21). Right away, He makes the disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to the other side. Then He sends the crowds away.

cards.question: Once the crowds are gone, Jesus goes up on the mountain by Himself to pray.

cards.text: Evening comes, and Jesus is up there alone. Meanwhile the boat is already far from land, getting beaten by the waves.

cards.question: The disciples' boat is getting beaten by the waves because the ___ is against it.

cards.text: Then, during the fourth watch of the night, Jesus goes out to them. That's so late, even my cookie dough has gone to bed.

cards.question: During the fourth watch of the night, how does Jesus get out to the disciples' boat?

cards.text: The disciples see Him walking on the sea, and they are TERRIFIED. Honestly, I'd scream too, and I scream when an oven timer goes off that I forgot I set.

cards.question: The terrified disciples cry out in fear. They think Jesus is a ___.
Jesus waits until the storm calms down before He says anything to the frightened disciples.

cards.text: Jesus speaks up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.” Then Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, calls back, “Lord, if it is You,” and asks Him for something.

cards.question: Out on the stormy sea, what does Peter ask Jesus to do?

answers.text: Command him to come on the water

cards.text: Jesus answers with one word: “Come.” So Peter gets down out of the boat.

cards.question: After Peter gets down out of the boat, he walks on the water and comes toward Jesus.

cards.text: Peter's out on the water, heading toward Jesus. Then he notices what's going on around him.

cards.question: Out on the water, Peter sees something, gets afraid and begins to sink. What does he see?

cards.text: Peter starts to sink and cries out, “Lord, save me!” Three words, no speech, which is exactly how I yell when a tray of cookies slides off the counter.

cards.question: As Peter sinks, Jesus ___ reaches out His hand and takes hold of him.

cards.text: Jesus tells him, “You of little faith,” and asks, “why did you doubt?” I bet Peter is very wet and very quiet right about now.

cards.question: Jesus and Peter are still out on the sea. When does the wind finally die down?

answers.text: When they climb back into the boat
When Peter cries out for help
When Jesus speaks to the wind

cards.question: The wind dies down, and everyone in the boat ___ Jesus, saying He is truly the ___ of God.

cards.text: They cross over and land at Gennesaret, and the men there recognize Jesus. Friend, nobody ever recognizes me, and I've got a mustache you can see from space.

cards.question: Once the men of Gennesaret recognize Jesus, they keep His visit to themselves.

cards.text: And here they come. People bring all the sick to Him.

cards.question: In Gennesaret, what do the people beg Jesus to let them do?

answers.text: Just touch the fringe of His cloak
Hear Him teach beside the sea

cards.question: In Gennesaret, only some of the people who touched Jesus were healed.

findings.problem: The card opens by retelling Matthew 14:29 ("Peter's out on the water, heading toward Jesus"), which stop 1 card 13 already covered, but it cites only Matthew 14:30. Either cite Matthew 14:29-30, or drop the first sentence and carry the moment forward instead of recapping it.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This is a which-thing question (what is against the boat). The wrong answer "tide" doesn't appear to be a real detail from the Bible's text. Replace it with something the Bible actually names, such as "currents" from Jonah 2:3 or another real detail.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: "The height of the waves" is too close to the right answer. The passage has already shown the waves pounding the boat (Matthew 14:24), and the wind is what drives them, so a baker could argue that seeing the waves is seeing the storm Peter feared. Replace it with a wrong answer that a baker can't argue is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The humor is mild throughout. Most jokes read like a nice dad being pleasant, not laugh-out-loud lines: "even my cookie dough has gone to bed" (stop 1 card 5) and "very wet and very quiet" (stop 2 card 5). The biggest moments get no reaction at all, such as Peter actually stepping onto the water (stop 1 cards 12 and 13) and the wind dropping as they climb into the boat. There is only one LOUD moment in the whole walkthrough.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Several story cards are plain narration with none of Papa Dorin's voice: stop 1 card 3, stop 1 card 12, stop 2 card 1 and stop 2 card 10.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The joke says Peter's cry "Lord, save me!" is "exactly how I yell when a tray of cookies slides off the counter." This can read as Papa Dorin using Peter's prayer to the Lord as his own reaction to dropped cookies. That trivializes a cry to Jesus, even though the joke is aimed at himself.
findings.question: Is it acceptable for a joke to compare a Bible character's prayer or cry to God with Papa Dorin's reaction to a trivial mishap? Or should comparisons to someone calling on the Lord be limited to the human side, such as the panic and the shortness of the words, without suggesting he says the prayer himself?
